summary: CVE-2026-25253. A link opened the control interface with an attacker gatewayUrl, which sent the gateway token to the attacker. Script in the victim's browser then opened a WebSocket to the local gateway with that token, turned off exec approval (exec.approvals.set), moved exec out of the sandbox (config.patch tools.exec.host) and ran a command on the host (node.invoke system.run).
decisive_reason: The command run on the host is the remote code execution.

stages.title: Build and stage the exploit script; the victim clicks the link and it runs in their browser
stages.basis: Attacker infrastructure and a script running in a browser tab. No agent turn, no tool call.

stages.title: Leak the gateway token through gatewayUrl, hijack a WebSocket to the local gateway, authenticate with the stolen token
stages.basis: Browser to gateway WebSocket traffic from another client. It is not a session event. Whether the gateway logs these connections, and whether ClawMetry's gateway log reader keeps such a line, is not checked in this tier.

stages.title: Turn off exec approval: exec.approvals.set {security: full, ask: off}
stages.basis: A gateway API call, not a tool call. This is also the one pre-action control ClawMetry drives for OpenClaw, and failure mode FM-1 shows ClawMetry does not put it back.

stages.title: Escape the sandbox: config.patch tools.exec.host = gateway
stages.basis: A gateway API call that changes OpenClaw's own configuration. Guard's workspace scan reads git config, editor tasks, agent hook settings and package manifests, not OpenClaw's configuration.

stages.title: Run a command on the host: node.invoke system.run
stages.basis: The command is sent through the gateway's node RPC, not through an agent turn, so no tool call reaches the session transcript Guard reads. Gateway log visibility is not checked in this tier.
